No. 2.summary: Charles VI to Windischgrätz: whether [Spain] and Orleans will in the end come to terms with one another again, and how one could free oneself entirely from the burden of the Barrier.

No. 3.summary: Beretti Landi, the Spanish envoy at The Hague, proposed in his court's name a marriage between one of the Emperor's children and Anjou's sons; Charles will stay on good terms with that court, but 'both are so small' that nothing is to be made known yet, an early trace of the Austro-Spanish marriage scheme of 1725.

No. 6.summary: To Windischgrätz as plenipotentiary at the Congress of Cambrai, on his talks with Beretti about a Spanish marriage: Beretti is 'embittered against me and Austria', but it is not bad to make use of him and show him every consideration.

system: The Emperor's private key R5018: each of 24 letters a number from 10 to 38 and a graphic sign, the vowels a second number; about 300 codes (39-210 and two-letter groups) for words and names; nulls 3-7 and 9.
